profile.name: Kemar Roach
profile.writeup:
There is a particular kind of fast bowler Barbados has always produced, tearaway quicks who make up for whatever they lack in height with raw pace and heart, and Kemar Roach fits that mould as well as anyone the island has sent out in the modern era. He first wore West Indies colours at the 2006 Under-19 World Cup, and the senior call-up followed not long after, with a T20I debut against Australia in 2008 and an ODI debut later that year.


His Test debut, though, came almost by accident. In 2009, a bitter pay dispute between the players and the board left West Indies fielding a severely weakened side against Bangladesh, and a 21-year-old Roach found himself thrown into the Test arena. He did not waste the chance, taking 13 wickets in the series, and when West Indies toured Australia that winter, he announced himself to the wider cricketing world by bowling with enough hostility to force Ricky Ponting into retiring hurt in Perth.


The years that followed cemented him as one of the side's most important bowlers. He took a hat-trick at the 2011 World Cup against the Netherlands, became the first West Indian in years to take 10 wickets in a Test in 2012, and kept piling up five-wicket hauls season after season. But his path was never entirely smooth. By 2016 he found himself out of the side altogether, left out ahead of a home series against India, and had to go back to domestic cricket to force his way back in.


He ground through a strong season before earning a recall for the 2017 tour of England. From there, he rebuilt himself into one of the side's most dependable performers once again, crossing 200 Test wickets in 2020 and continuing to lead the attack into his 30s. Alongside all of this, he built a long second career in English county cricket, first with Worcestershire and later a 5-year run with Surrey that brought 3 County Championship titles, before a late move to Durham in 2026. There was IPL cricket too, a big money move to Deccan Chargers in 2010 and later a spell with Sunrisers Hyderabad.


Just when it seemed his international story might be winding down, it took one more turn. In mid 2025, the West Indies board made it clear he was no longer part of their plans, and he was left out of a home series despite still ranking among the country's leading wicket-takers in Test history. It looked, for a while, like the end. Then injuries elsewhere in the attack brought him back for a tour of New Zealand that November. In a tense final day there, he played one of the most memorable innings of his career with the bat, grinding out an unbeaten 58 off 233 balls in a marathon stand with Justin Greaves to help save the match.


A few months later, in June 2026, he reached one of fast bowling's rarest landmarks for a West Indian as he became only the fourth pacer in the country's history to take 300 Test wickets, nearly 17 years after that chaotic, improvised debut against Bangladesh.
